intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative certificate.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most celebrated Great Walks, traversing alpine meadows, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The 32km trail offers stunning views of Lake Harris, Routeburn Falls, and the Darran Mountains. Book a guided day section or multi-day hut pass.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: Walk one of the South Island's most rewarding and accessible alpine hikes through Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. This 10km return trail crosses three swing bridges and rewards hikers with jaw-dropping views of Mount Cook, the Hooker Glacier terminal lake, and floating icebergs. Completely free and suitable for most fitness levels.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Wilderness Walk Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the dramatic fiords of Milford Sound at water level, passing beneath towering 1200-meter cliffs and Stirling Falls. Combine with a guided rainforest walk through ancient podocarp forest to spot native wildlife including Fiordland crested penguins and fur seals. A truly immersive Fiordland experience.

experiences.name: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools and Spa
experiences.description: Relax and recover tired hiking muscles in the geothermal mineral pools of Hanmer Springs, a charming alpine village surrounded by pine forests and mountains. Choose from outdoor thermal pools ranging from 36°C to 42°C, private rock pools, and hydrotherapy jets. A perfect mid-trip recovery day blending wellness with scenic mountain culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

Completely free and suitable for most fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 - no morning activities scheduled. Rest and recover from flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Freshen up and take a leisurely walk along Queenstown Bay waterfront to get oriented with the town. Visit the free Queenstown Gardens nearby for a relaxing stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Explore central Queenstown on foot. Browse the Queenstown Night Markets (open Sunday–Thursday) for cheap eats and local atmosphere. Pick up groceries from Countdown Supermarket for budget self-catering during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport cafe upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap bite at Fergburger (iconic Queenstown burger joint, ~NZD 12-15) after check-in
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market food stalls (NZD 8-12 per dish) or self-cater from supermarket groceries

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities only begin after 13:00 arrival. Focus on settling in and getting oriented. Buy a prepaid SIM card at the airport for data/maps. Confirm bungee jumping bookings if not already done.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Ben Lomond Track from Queenstown — a stunning free hike with panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables. Start early from the trailhead near the Queenstown Gondola base (approx 4-5 hours return to summit).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Ben Lomond and cool down with a swim at the free Frankton Beach on Lake Wakatipu. Alternatively, explore the free Queenstown Gardens trails.
day_by_day.evening: Relax back at accommodation. Cook a simple meal using supermarket supplies. Review gear and prepare for bungee jumping the next day.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at accommodation before the hike
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and snacks for the trail
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or stir-fry at accommodation (NZD 5-8 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is free and one of the best hikes near Queenstown. Wear layers as summit can be cold and windy even in November. Carry at least 2L of water. Trail is well-marked from Queenstown town centre.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — the highest bungee jump in New Zealand at 134m, operated by AJ Hackett and located in the Nevis Valley (very close to your accommodation). This is a bucket-list experience. Book in advance for best pricing (~NZD 275).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, recover with a scenic drive through the Nevis Valley. Take in the dramatic schist rock landscapes. Visit the Nevis Bluff viewpoint for free panoramic photos.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Queenstown for a celebratory budget dinner. Stroll along the lakefront and watch the sunset over The Remarkables mountain range.

meals.breakfast: Light self-catered breakfast — avoid heavy meals before the jump
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and energy bars for the Nevis Valley day
meals.dinner: Winnies Pizza or The Cow restaurant for affordable wood-fired pizza (~NZD 18-22 per pizza, shareable)

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy is the flagship experience given your accommodation location. Book well in advance as slots fill up. AJ Hackett provides transport from Queenstown town centre to the Nevis platform. Minimum weight requirements apply (45kg). GoPro footage available as an add-on.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus to Glenorchy (45 min from Queenstown, free to drive). Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway — a flat, easy 1.5-hour loop through wetlands with stunning mountain reflections. Completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the start of the Routeburn Track for a free day hike to the Routeburn Flats (approx 4 hours return). Stunning beech forest and mountain scenery without paying for the full multi-day track.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Visit the free Queenstown Hill Time Walk for sunset views over the town and lake.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before driving to Glenorchy
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Routeburn Flats — sandwiches and fruit from supermarket
meals.dinner: Vudu Larder & Cafe or self-cater. Budget option: Pak'nSave supermarket deli items (~NZD 8-10)

day_by_day.notes: Glenorchy is used as a filming location for Lord of the Rings — look out for iconic scenery. The road to Glenorchy is one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand and is free. Fill up on petrol in Queenstown as there are no stations in Glenorchy.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Wanaka (approx 1 hour from Queenstown). Walk the free Rob Roy Glacier Track (4-5 hours return, 10km) — one of the most spectacular day hikes in New Zealand featuring a hanging glacier, waterfalls and alpine meadows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Rob Roy. Visit the famous Wanaka Tree (lone willow tree in Lake Wanaka) for photos. Walk the free Outlet Track along the lake shore.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Wanaka town. Visit Puzzling World for a budget-friendly quirky attraction (~NZD 16) or simply enjoy the free lakefront sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before the drive to Wanaka
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the Rob Roy Track — essential as there are no cafes at the trailhead
meals.dinner: Federal Diner in Wanaka for affordable meals (~NZD 15-20) or pick up supplies from New World supermarket in Wanaka

day_by_day.notes: Rob Roy Glacier Track requires a river crossing which may be high in November (spring melt). Check conditions at the DOC visitor centre in Wanaka before heading out. The track is in Mount Aspiring National Park — entry is free. Stay overnight in Wanaka if budget allows to save driving time.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Mount Iron Track in Wanaka (2 hours return, free) for 360-degree views of the lakes and Southern Alps. A great moderate hike with minimal effort for maximum reward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Haast Pass (approx 2 hours from Wanaka). Stop at the free Thunder Creek Falls (15-minute walk) and Blue Pools (30-minute walk through stunning beech forest). Continue toward the West Coast.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Franz Josef or Fox Glacier township. Check into a budget hostel (YHA or similar, ~NZD 30-40/night dorm). Explore the small glacier town.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered in Wanaka before departing
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the Haast Pass drive — eat at Thunder Creek Falls picnic area
meals.dinner: The Landing restaurant in Franz Josef or self-cater from the local Four Square store

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass drive is one of the most scenic routes in New Zealand — allow extra time for stops. Blue Pools are a must-see. November weather on the West Coast can be wet — pack a waterproof jacket. The West Coast receives significantly more rainfall than Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk (free, 2-3 hours return). Walk as close to the glacier terminal face as permitted by DOC. Stunning blue ice and dramatic valley scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 30 minutes south to Fox Glacier. Walk the free Fox Glacier Valley Track (2 hours return) for another perspective on the glaciers. Visit Lake Matheson for the famous mirror reflection of Mount Cook and Mount Tasman (~30 min walk, free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Franz Josef. Relax at the accommodation. If budget allows, visit the Glacier Hot Pools (~NZD 35) to soak tired muscles.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Fox Glacier or Lake Matheson picnic area
meals.dinner: Blue Ice Restaurant in Franz Josef for budget meals or self-cater at hostel kitchen

day_by_day.notes: Both glacier walks are free DOC tracks. Do not attempt to go beyond safety barriers — the glaciers are actively retreating and the terrain is unstable. Lake Matheson is best photographed in early morning for still water reflections, but the afternoon visit is still beautiful. November is a good time before peak summer crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north along the stunning West Coast to Punakaiki (approx 2.5 hours). Visit the Pancake Rocks and Blowholes at Dolomite Point — a free and extraordinary coastal geological formation. Walk the 30-minute loop track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving north to Hanmer Springs (approx 3-3.5 hours via Lewis Pass). The Lewis Pass route is free, scenic and passes through native beech forest. Stop at Maruia Falls for a quick free photo stop.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hanmer Springs. Check into budget accommodation (Top 10 Holiday Park or Hanmer Backpackers, ~NZD 30-45/night). Explore the charming village.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the long drive day
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Punakaiki or on the road
meals.dinner: Hanmer Springs has several affordable cafes — try Powerhouse Cafe or self-cater at accommodation

day_by_day.notes: Today is a long driving day (~5-6 hours total). Start early. Punakaiki is worth every minute — the blowholes are most dramatic at high tide, check tide times in advance. The Lewis Pass route (SH7) is less travelled and very scenic. Fill up petrol before leaving the West Coast as stations are sparse.

day_by_day.morning: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools and Spa — soak in the geothermal mineral pools to recover tired hiking muscles. Entry fee is approximately NZD 25-30 for adults. Visit early to avoid crowds and enjoy the peaceful mountain setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Conical Hill Track in Hanmer Springs (1.5 hours return, free) for panoramic views of the Hanmer Basin and surrounding mountains. Alternatively, walk the free Woodland Walk through the exotic forest plantation.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Hanmer Springs village. Browse the small shops and relax. Prepare for the drive to Christchurch the next day.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Grab a budget bite at Hanmer Springs Bakery or pack your own
meals.dinner: Monteiths Brewery Bar in Hanmer Springs for affordable pub meals (~NZD 18-25) or self-cater

day_by_day.notes: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools is one of the listed available experiences — a perfect recovery day after days of hiking and adventure. The pools include multiple outdoor thermal pools at varying temperatures. Towel hire available on-site. The village has a relaxed, charming atmosphere ideal for a rest day.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Hanmer Springs to Christchurch (approx 1.5 hours). Check in to budget accommodation in Christchurch (Base Backpackers or Jailhouse Accommodation, ~NZD 30-40/night). Explore the free Christchurch Botanic Gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Transitional Cathedral (Cardboard Cathedral) and the ongoing Christchurch city rebuild — fascinating urban regeneration story. Explore the free Re:START Mall and arts precinct. Visit the free Canterbury Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Avon River in the evening light. Visit the vibrant Christchurch Night Noodle Markets or explore the local bar and cafe scene on Victoria Street.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered or grab a coffee and pastry on the road from Hanmer
meals.lunch: Christchurch Farmers Market (Saturdays) or grab cheap eats from the city food trucks (~NZD 10-15)
meals.dinner: Night Noodle Markets or Riverside Market food hall for affordable diverse cuisine (~NZD 12-18)

day_by_day.notes: Christchurch has transformed dramatically since the 2011 earthquake — the city rebuild and street art scene is genuinely fascinating and free to explore. The Botanic Gardens are among the best in New Zealand and completely free. Use the free Christchurch City Loop bus to get around the central city.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (approx 3.5 hours from Christchurch via SH1 and SH8 through the Mackenzie Basin). Stop at Lake Tekapo on the way — walk to the Church of the Good Shepherd (free) and enjoy the stunning turquoise lake views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mount Cook Village. Begin the Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier — one of the South Island's most rewarding accessible alpine hikes. The 10km return track features swing bridges, glacier views and stunning Aoraki/Mount Cook scenery. Allow 3-4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset alpenglow on Aoraki/Mount Cook from the village. The Mackenzie Basin is a Dark Sky Reserve — spend time stargazing after dark (completely free and extraordinary).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the drive
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Mueller Glacier viewpoint at the end of the Hooker Valley Track
meals.dinner: Self-cater at the DOC campground kitchen or grab takeaways from the small store at Mount Cook Village (limited options — bring supplies from Christchurch or Tekapo)

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is one of the listed available experiences and is a highlight of the entire South Island. It is free, well-maintained and suitable for most fitness levels. Stay at the DOC White Horse Hill Campground (~NZD 15/night) for the most budget-friendly option near the track. Bring all food supplies from Tekapo as Mount Cook Village is very expensive. November offers long daylight hours — perfect for evening stargazing.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Sealy Tarns Track from White Horse Hill Campground (3-4 hours return) for elevated views over the Hooker Valley and Mueller Glacier. A steeper and more challenging hike than the Hooker Valley Track but incredibly rewarding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Queenstown via Twizel and Omarama (approx 3 hours). Stop at Lake Pukaki viewpoint for iconic Aoraki/Mount Cook reflections in the vivid blue glacial lake — completely free and one of the most photographed spots in New Zealand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown/Nevis Valley accommodation. Celebrate the final full night with a walk along the Queenstown lakefront and a treat dinner out.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at campground before the morning hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Sealy Tarns Track or at Lake Pukaki picnic area
meals.dinner: Treat yourself at Fergburger (Queenstown institution) or Rata restaurant for a budget splurge on the final evening (~NZD 25-35)

day_by_day.notes: Sealy Tarns is steeper than Hooker Valley — poles recommended. The Lake Pukaki viewpoint is best in clear weather when Aoraki/Mount Cook is visible — November generally offers good visibility. The drive back to Queenstown through the Mackenzie Basin is beautiful and passes through classic New Zealand high country sheep farming territory.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Nevis Valley/Queenstown area. Take a leisurely walk around the Queenstown Bay waterfront or revisit a favourite spot. Pack and check out of accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — visit the free Queenstown Hill summit walk for final panoramic views, or browse the Queenstown Arts and Crafts Market for affordable souvenirs. Head to the airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Queenstown Airport. Reflect on an incredible 13-day South Island adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast or grab coffee and a muffin at a local cafe
meals.lunch: Airport cafe or a final Fergburger to go
meals.dinner: On the plane or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 10:00-11:00am. Queenstown Airport is only 10 minutes from the town centre. Allow extra time for security. Use any remaining NZD cash on last-minute snacks or a small souvenir. Consider buying Manuka honey or local chocolate as affordable gifts. Return any hired gear before heading to the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Queenstown Airport to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay (~45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the Queenstown lakefront to get your bearings. Enjoy views of The Remarkables mountain range across Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown town centre. Browse the waterfront and get oriented with local shops and restaurants. Light exploration of Church Street and the pedestrian mall.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Queenstown Airport or a café near the waterfront such as Vudu Café & Larder — great cabinet food and coffee (~NZD 18–25)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant on The Mall — mid-range fine casual dining by chef Josh Emett, celebrating New Zealand produce. Mains ~NZD 38–48. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from long-haul travel. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings (Nevis Bungy, Routeburn, kayak combo) and check weather forecasts. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — depart from central Queenstown on the AJ Hackett shuttle (~30 min to the Nevis platform). Experience New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. The jump itself takes around 3 hours including transfer, briefing, and jump time. Adrenaline levels: maximum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Recover with a walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront or a gentle stroll up to the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2–3 hrs return, moderate) for panoramic views of the Remarkables and Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in Queenstown. Visit Skyline Gondola for sunset views over the lake (optional ~NZD 35) or simply enjoy the town atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or nearby — try Bespoke Kitchen on Isle Street for healthy bowls and eggs (~NZD 18–24)
meals.lunch: Fergburger on Shotover Street — Queenstown's iconic burger institution. Expect a short queue. Burgers ~NZD 16–22.
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant — cozy stone-walled restaurant serving hearty pasta and pizza, perfect post-bungy comfort food. Mains ~NZD 28–36.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable, close-toed shoes for the bungy. Avoid heavy meals before the jump. Bring a GoPro or purchase the official jump video/photo package (~NZD 50–80). Minimum weight 45 kg, maximum 127 kg.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Glenorchy (45 min from Queenstown along a stunning lakeside road). Stop at Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway for a short 30-minute flat walk with incredible mountain reflections. This is the gateway to the Routeburn Track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Glenorchy area. Hike the Glenorchy Lagoon and Paradise area (2–3 hrs, easy-moderate) — a flat valley walk through beech forest and wetlands with views of Mount Earnslaw. Optional jet boat on the Dart River (~NZD 149).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Quiet evening to pack and prepare gear for the multi-day Routeburn Track starting tomorrow. Check and repack your tramping gear — waterproof layers, boots, trekking poles, snacks.

meals.breakfast: Accommodation breakfast or Vudu Café in Queenstown before driving to Glenorchy
meals.lunch: Glenorchy Café — casual lakeside café with sandwiches, pies, and good coffee. Lunch ~NZD 16–22.
meals.dinner: Pub dinner at Sherwood Queenstown — relaxed gastropub atmosphere with locally sourced seasonal menu. Mains ~NZD 32–42.

day_by_day.notes: Stop at a Queenstown supermarket (New World or Countdown) to purchase 2 days of hut food and snacks for the Routeburn Track. Confirm hut bookings with DOC. November is shoulder-to-peak season — weather can be mixed, pack layers.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day 1 — Transfer by shuttle from Queenstown to the Routeburn Shelter (Glenorchy end) at approximately 8:00–9:00 am (~NZD 45 one-way, book with Trackhopper or similar). Begin hiking from the Routeburn Shelter. The first section follows the Routeburn River through ancient beech forest (7.5 km, ~2.5 hrs to Routeburn Flats Hut).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Routeburn Flats Hut up to Routeburn Falls Hut (2.5 km, ~1.5 hrs, steeper climb with waterfalls). Arrive at the hut by early afternoon. Explore the area around the hut and the spectacular Routeburn Falls viewpoint just above.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Routeburn Falls Hut (DOC Great Walks Hut, ~NZD 75/night). Cook your hut dinner, socialise with fellow trampers, and enjoy the extraordinary alpine twilight. Sunset views from the hut are world-class.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation before shuttle departure — toast, eggs, or muesli
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars, fruit prepared the night before
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hut meal — lightweight dehydrated meal or instant noodles with tuna, purchased from Queenstown supermarket

day_by_day.notes: Total Day 1 walking: ~10 km, approximately 4–5 hours. Elevation gain ~480 m to Routeburn Falls Hut. Carry at least 2L of water. Hut has gas cookers, toilets, and sleeping platforms. No showers. Trekking poles highly recommended for the climb to Falls Hut.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day 2 — Early start from Routeburn Falls Hut. Climb above the bushline to the Harris Saddle (1,255 m) — the highest point of the track. Spectacular 360-degree alpine views on a clear day. Optional side trip to Conical Hill (add 1.5 hrs return) for even more dramatic panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Harris Saddle to Lake Mackenzie Hut (9 km from Falls Hut, ~3.5–4.5 hrs total). Arrive at the stunning Lake Mackenzie — a glacially carved lake surrounded by mountain peaks. Rest, swim if brave (cold!), and enjoy the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Stay at Lake Mackenzie Hut (~NZD 75/night). Evening socialising in the hut. Watch alpenglow on the peaks at dusk. Rest well — tomorrow is the final push.

meals.breakfast: Hot oats or muesli with powdered milk cooked in the hut — fuel up for the big alpine section
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Harris Saddle or Conical Hill — crackers, cheese, salami, chocolate
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hut meal — dehydrated camping meal (Mountain House or Back Country Cuisine, purchased in Queenstown)

day_by_day.notes: Total Day 2 walking: ~9 km, approximately 3.5–5 hours. The Harris Saddle section can be exposed and cold even in November — always carry a warm layer and rain jacket. Check the weather board at Routeburn Falls Hut before departing. Avalanche risk is low in November but check with DOC.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day 3 — Hike the final section from Lake Mackenzie Hut to The Divide (8.5 km, ~3 hrs). Pass through Earland Falls (a spectacular 174 m waterfall), beech forest, and subalpine terrain. Arrive at The Divide carpark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch the pre-booked shuttle from The Divide back to Queenstown (~2.5 hrs via Te Anau). Arrive Queenstown mid-to-late afternoon. Check back into Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Shower, do laundry, and decompress.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Queenstown after completing the Routeburn Track. Enjoy a well-earned restaurant meal and a local craft beer or glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Hot hut breakfast — oats or instant coffee and muesli before the final day's hike
meals.lunch: Finish remaining trail snacks on the hike out, or grab a pie at The Divide if available
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery on Marine Parade — upscale casual with excellent Central Otago lamb and beef. Mains ~NZD 40–55. A well-deserved treat.

day_by_day.notes: Book The Divide shuttle in advance with Trackhopper, Info & Track (Queenstown) or Naked Bus. Total Routeburn Track: ~32 km over 3 days. A genuine Great Walk achievement. Rest legs tonight — more hiking ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning in Queenstown. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and do any necessary laundry or gear maintenance. Optional: gentle walk along the Queenstown Gardens (1 hr loop, flat) to stretch the legs without strain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a scenic bus to Arrowtown (~25 min from Queenstown). Explore this beautifully preserved 1860s gold-rush town. Walk the Arrow River Bridges Trail (2 hrs, easy) along the river through the historic Chinese Settlement. Browse the boutique shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Sunset drinks at a lakefront bar. Plan the upcoming Te Anau/Milford Sound leg of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Extended breakfast at accommodation or Bespoke Kitchen — treat yourself to a full brunch after the Routeburn
meals.lunch: Arrowtown — Fork & Tap gastropub or Provisions of Arrowtown for excellent sandwiches, salads, and pies. ~NZD 20–28.
meals.dinner: Queenstown — Wai Waterfront Restaurant for fresh South Island salmon and seafood with lake views. Mains ~NZD 35–48.

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day before the Milford Sound section. Arrowtown is one of New Zealand's most charming towns and a great low-effort afternoon. Stock up on any supplies needed for the Milford leg. Book accommodation in Te Anau tonight if not already done.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Te Anau (~2 hrs, 170 km). The drive passes through the Kingston Flyer plains and Fiordland's dramatic entrance. Check into Te Anau accommodation (mid-range options: Fiordland Hotel or Te Anau Lodge ~NZD 150–200/night). Walk the Te Anau lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Te Anau Glowworm Caves cruise (Real Journeys, ~NZD 89/adult, 2 hrs) — boat across Lake Te Anau to the hidden cave system with thousands of glowworms. A magical and unique Fiordland experience. Book in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Te Anau. Early night in preparation for the big Milford Sound day tomorrow. Check the Milford Road webcam and weather forecast.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Queenstown accommodation before departing, or stop at a café in Kingston (~1 hr into drive)
meals.lunch: Redcliff Restaurant & Bar in Te Anau for a casual lunch — good burgers and local venison dishes. ~NZD 22–32.
meals.dinner: Miles Better Pies & Café or The Fat Duck Restaurant in Te Anau — hearty, warming Fiordland-style meals. Mains ~NZD 28–38.

day_by_day.notes: Fill up with petrol in Te Anau before any Milford Road travel — no fuel stations on the Milford Road. Confirm tomorrow's kayak and wilderness walk combo booking. The Milford Road (SH94) is 120 km and takes ~2 hrs — an attraction in itself.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Kayak and Wilderness Walk Combo — Depart Te Anau early (~6:30 am) to drive the Milford Road to Milford Sound (arrive ~8:30 am). Begin the guided kayak portion, paddling through the fiord at water level beneath 1,200-metre granite walls. Pass Stirling Falls and look for dolphins, seals, and penguins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the wilderness walk section of the combo through ancient rainforest along the fiord edge. Enjoy lunch at Milford Sound Lodge or packed lunch. Afternoon free time to explore the Milford Sound foreshore and visitor area. Optional: add a short cruise (~NZD 75) for different perspectives.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau (~2 hrs). Arrive early evening. Dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before 6:30 am departure — prepare the night before
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or Milford Sound Lodge café — basic sandwiches and hot drinks. Budget ~NZD 18–25.
meals.dinner: Fiordland Brewery in Te Anau — great local craft beers and hearty pub meals. Mains ~NZD 28–36.

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Sound Kayak and Wilderness Walk Combo typically runs 5–6 hours. Wear layers — the fiord is cooler than inland even in November. Sandflies are notorious at Milford — bring strong insect repellent. Waterproof your camera/phone. This is one of the world's great natural experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau toward Mount Cook (Aoraki) via the Mackenzie Basin — a spectacular ~4 hr drive through Fiordland, past Lake Pukaki (stunning turquoise glacial lake), and into the Mackenzie Country. Stop at Lake Pukaki viewpoint for photos of Aoraki/Mount Cook reflected in the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Aoraki/Mount Cook Village. Check into The Hermitage Hotel or Mount Cook YHA (~NZD 120–200/night). Begin the Hooker Valley Track — one of New Zealand's most rewarding alpine hikes. The 10 km return walk crosses three swing bridges and passes Mueller Lake before reaching Hooker Lake and its glacier terminal face.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mount Cook Village. Enjoy the extraordinary stargazing — the Mackenzie Basin is an International Dark Sky Reserve, one of the best stargazing locations on Earth.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Lake Pukaki or en route — stop at Twizel (~NZD 15–20 at a local café)
meals.dinner: The Hermitage Hotel — Old Mountaineers' Café for casual dining with incredible Aoraki views. Mains ~NZD 30–42.

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track (10 km return, ~3 hrs, easy-moderate) is best done in the afternoon light for photography. Flat track with swing bridges. November weather at 760 m elevation can be changeable — bring a windproof layer. The track ends at Hooker Lake with icebergs floating from the glacier — extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier (if not completed yesterday, or explore the Red Tarns Track as an alternative — 1.5 hrs return, steep but rewarding views over the entire valley and Mount Cook). Alternatively, take the Kea Point Track (2 hrs return, easy) to Mueller Glacier viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Mount Cook toward Hanmer Springs (~3.5 hrs via Inland Scenic Route through the Mackenzie Basin and Lewis Pass). Arrive Hanmer Springs mid-to-late afternoon. Check into Hanmer Springs accommodation (Heritage Hanmer Springs or a local B&B ~NZD 140–180/night).
day_by_day.evening: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools and Spa — soak tired hiking muscles in the geothermal mineral pools. The complex has multiple pools at varying temperatures, plus private pools and spa treatments. Open until 9 pm (~NZD 25 adult entry). A perfect recovery evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at The Hermitage before departing Mount Cook
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the road or stop in Culverden (~1 hr from Hanmer) at a local café
meals.dinner: Monteiths Brewery Bar in Hanmer Springs — relaxed atmosphere, good burgers and craft beer. Mains ~NZD 26–36.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Mount Cook to Hanmer Springs via Lewis Pass is one of New Zealand's great inland drives — expect stunning high country scenery. Hanmer Springs is a charming alpine village perfectly positioned as a recovery stop. Book spa treatments in advance if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Morning return to Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools for a final soak, or explore the Hanmer Forest Park walking tracks. The Majuba Track (3 hrs loop, moderate) through pine and native forest is an excellent option for those not yet tired of hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Hanmer Springs to Christchurch (~1.5 hrs, 135 km). Check into Christchurch city accommodation (mid-range: Sudima Hotel, Novotel, or a boutique guesthouse ~NZD 160–200/night). Explore the Christchurch Botanic Gardens (free, 30 hectares of stunning gardens along the Avon River).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Christchurch's vibrant post-earthquake rebuild. Visit the Cardboard Cathedral (Te Puna o Waiwhetu) and the Container Mall (Re:START). Enjoy the creative, resilient energy of this reinvented city.

meals.breakfast: Hanmer Springs — The Powerhouse Café for a leisurely final morning breakfast. ~NZD 18–26.
meals.lunch: Christchurch — C1 Espresso in the city centre, famous for its sliders and quirky atmosphere. ~NZD 20–28.
meals.dinner: Christchurch — Gatherings Restaurant on Colombo Street for outstanding seasonal New Zealand cuisine. Mains ~NZD 38–52. A fitting final dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Christchurch is a fascinating city to end the trip — its post-2011 earthquake rebuild has produced some of New Zealand's most innovative architecture and hospitality. Allow time to simply wander and absorb the city's unique resilience and creativity.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Christchurch. Visit the Canterbury Museum (free) for excellent natural history and South Island Māori cultural exhibits. Walk along the Avon River Precinct (Otākaro) — a beautiful riverside park created on earthquake-cleared land.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: visit the International Antarctic Centre near the airport (~NZD 39, 2 hrs) for a fascinating look at New Zealand's role as the gateway to Antarctica. Transfer to Christchurch International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Christchurch. Reflect on an extraordinary 13 days across one of the world's most spectacular destinations.

meals.breakfast: Christchurch — Café Valentino or Addington Coffee Co-op for a final South Island brunch. ~NZD 18–25.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the airport or at the International Antarctic Centre café before check-in
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check out of accommodation by 10–11 am. Christchurch Airport is 10 minutes from the city centre. Allow at least 2.5 hours before international departure. Consider purchasing last-minute New Zealand souvenirs at the airport duty-free — Whittaker's chocolate, Manuka honey, and Merino wool products make excellent gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative certificate.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most celebrated Great Walks, traversing alpine meadows, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The 32km trail offers stunning views of Lake Harris, Routeburn Falls, and the Darran Mountains. Book a guided day section or multi-day hut pass.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: Walk one of the South Island's most rewarding and accessible alpine hikes through Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. This 10km return trail crosses three swing bridges and rewards hikers with jaw-dropping views of Mount Cook, the Hooker Glacier terminal lake, and floating icebergs. Completely free and suitable for most fitness levels.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Wilderness Walk Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the dramatic fiords of Milford Sound at water level, passing beneath towering 1200-meter cliffs and Stirling Falls. Combine with a guided rainforest walk through ancient podocarp forest to spot native wildlife including Fiordland crested penguins and fur seals. A truly immersive Fiordland experience.

experiences.name: Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools and Spa
experiences.description: Relax and recover tired hiking muscles in the geothermal mineral pools of Hanmer Springs, a charming alpine village surrounded by pine forests and mountains. Choose from outdoor thermal pools ranging from 36°C to 42°C, private rock pools, and hydrotherapy jets. A perfect mid-trip recovery day blending wellness with scenic mountain culture.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and settle into the boutique property. Enjoy a leisurely orientation walk around the Nevis Valley surroundings, taking in the dramatic schist rock gorge landscape and river views. Unwind on the private terrace with a welcome glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle first evening in Queenstown. Stroll along the lakefront promenade at Lake Wakatipu and explore the vibrant Queenstown town centre. Dinner at a top Queenstown restaurant to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light grazing platter and welcome drinks provided at the boutique stay upon check-in
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro — celebrated farm-to-table cuisine paired with estate-grown Central Otago wines in a stunning vineyard setting near Queenstown

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged. Confirm luggage is sent directly to the boutique stay. Allow time to adjust to time zone — keep the first evening relaxed. November is late spring in New Zealand, expect long daylight hours and mild temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay, take a scenic morning hike along the Crown Range Road trails above Queenstown. The elevated ridge walk offers sweeping panoramic views over the Wakatipu Basin, the Remarkables mountain range, and the Nevis Valley below — a perfect gentle warm-up hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Queenstown for a private guided tour of the Skyline Gondola and Bob's Peak. Enjoy lunch at the summit restaurant with 360-degree views. Spend the afternoon exploring Queenstown's adventure and boutique shopping scene at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at Perky's Floating Bar on the Queenstown waterfront, followed by a premium dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — locally sourced eggs, artisan breads, fresh fruit, and Central Otago honey
meals.lunch: Stratosfare Restaurant at Skyline Queenstown — buffet with panoramic lake and mountain views
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant by Josh Emett — one of Queenstown's finest restaurants, celebrating New Zealand produce with a refined contemporary menu

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable trail shoes for the morning ridge walk. The Crown Range area can be breezy even in November — bring a light windproof layer. Book Rata Restaurant well in advance as it is consistently fully booked.

day_by_day.morning: The iconic Nevis Bungy Jump experience — leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. A dedicated luxury transfer departs from Queenstown to the Nevis High Wire site. Pre-jump safety briefing and harness fitting with professional instructors. The 8.5-second freefall is an adrenaline experience unlike any other in New Zealand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the boutique stay for a well-deserved recovery. Enjoy the property's private amenities — hot tub, outdoor terrace, and massage if available on-site. Alternatively, book a 60-minute sports recovery massage at a Queenstown day spa such as Eforea Spa at Hilton.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the day's achievement with a premium dinner and fine wine pairing in Queenstown.

meals.breakfast: Hearty full gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — fuel up before the jump with high-protein options including smoked salmon, eggs your way, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box provided by the boutique stay, enjoyed at the Nevis site or on return
meals.dinner: The Bunker Restaurant — Queenstown's most intimate fine dining experience, hidden in a laneway, offering an exceptional tasting menu with New Zealand wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy Jump requires participants to meet weight restrictions (45–127 kg). Avoid eating a very heavy meal immediately before the jump. Video and photo packages are available on-site — highly recommended to capture the moment. Weather can occasionally delay operations; have a flexible backup plan.

day_by_day.morning: Private scenic helicopter flight from Queenstown over Fiordland, landing at a remote alpine location for a private guided wilderness walk. Explore untouched beech forest and alpine meadows inaccessible by road — a truly exclusive South Island experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fly into Te Anau, the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Check in or drop bags at a luxury lodge near Te Anau (day stop en route). Explore the shores of Lake Te Anau and visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves by private guided boat tour.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Te Anau surroundings and enjoy a relaxed lakeside dinner as preparation for the multi-day Routeburn Track experience beginning tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch provided by the helicopter operator, enjoyed at the alpine landing site
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant, Te Anau — a beloved local institution serving hearty New Zealand cuisine including venison, lamb, and fresh South Island seafood in a warm cottage setting

day_by_day.notes: Private helicopter experiences must be booked well in advance through operators such as Over The Top Helicopters or Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters. Te Anau Glowworm Caves tours are run by Real Journeys — book the private guided option for an exclusive experience. Pack bags for the Routeburn Track tonight — only essentials in a daypack.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Routeburn Track Great Walk — one of New Zealand's most celebrated multi-day hikes. Private guided departure from the Routeburn Shelter trailhead. Hike through ancient podocarp and beech forest along the Routeburn River, crossing swing bridges and passing dramatic waterfalls. Arrive at Routeburn Flats Hut area for a rest stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the ascent through increasingly dramatic alpine terrain toward Routeburn Falls. The falls themselves are a spectacular highlight — a powerful cascade tumbling from the alpine heights. Arrive at Routeburn Falls Hut (premium guided group accommodation or private hut booking) and settle in.
day_by_day.evening: Guided interpretation of the alpine ecosystem by your private guide around the hut. Enjoy a sunset view from above the bushline looking back over the Hollyford Valley. Communal hut dinner with fellow trampers.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet packed breakfast prepared by the guide before the trailhead departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch enjoyed at Routeburn Flats — artisan wraps, premium snacks, energy bars, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Premium guided group dinner at Routeburn Falls Hut — hot nutritious meals prepared by the guide including hearty New Zealand-style stews and dessert

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track requires advance Great Walks hut booking through DOC (Department of Conservation). For a premium experience, book through a licensed guided operator such as Ultimate Hikes who provide private guided Routeburn experiences with superior catering and guiding. Total day distance approximately 11 km. Pack rain gear regardless of forecast — Fiordland weather is notoriously changeable.

day_by_day.morning: Day 2 of the Routeburn Track. Rise early for sunrise above the bushline — an extraordinary alpine light show. Begin the climb from Routeburn Falls Hut above the treeline to the Harris Saddle at 1,255 meters. The panoramic views from Harris Saddle across Fiordland and the Darran Mountains are among the finest in New Zealand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional side trip to Conical Hill summit (additional 45-minute return from Harris Saddle) for 360-degree views on a clear day. Descend toward Lake Mackenzie through stunning alpine terrain. Arrive at Lake Mackenzie Hut — spectacularly situated above a turquoise glacial lake.
day_by_day.evening: Relax by the lake shore. The reflection of the Emily Peaks in Lake Mackenzie at dusk is one of the South Island's most magical scenes. Guided evening discussion on Fiordland geology and ecology.

meals.breakfast: Hot cooked breakfast at Routeburn Falls Hut — oats, eggs, and hot drinks prepared by the guide
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Harris Saddle — premium packed lunch with hot thermos soup provided by the guide
meals.dinner: Premium guided dinner at Lake Mackenzie Hut — fresh pasta, New Zealand lamb, and dessert with hot beverages

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be extremely exposed and cold even in November — full waterproof and windproof layers essential. The Conical Hill side trip is highly recommended in clear conditions but should be skipped in poor visibility. Total day distance approximately 11 km with significant elevation gain.

day_by_day.morning: Day 3 of the Routeburn Track — the final section. Depart Lake Mackenzie Hut and hike through the Hollyford Face, a dramatic traverse with cliff-edge views over the Hollyford Valley thousands of meters below. Pass through the Earland Falls area — a stunning 174-meter waterfall cascade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the Routeburn Track at the Divide, the lowest alpine pass in Fiordland. Private vehicle transfer arranged to meet the group and transfer to Milford Sound for the next chapter of the journey. Check in at the Milford Sound Lodge — the only accommodation within the Milford Sound area.
day_by_day.evening: First views of Milford Sound at dusk — Mitre Peak reflected in the still fiord waters is one of the world's great natural spectacles. Quiet evening at the lodge to rest after three days of hiking.

meals.breakfast: Hot cooked breakfast at Lake Mackenzie Hut before departure
meals.lunch: Celebratory trail lunch at the Divide to mark the completion of the Routeburn Track
meals.dinner: Milford Sound Lodge dining room — locally sourced New Zealand cuisine with fiord views; alternatively a premium packed dinner if arriving late

day_by_day.notes: The Divide to Milford Sound transfer takes approximately 1 hour via the Homer Tunnel. Milford Sound Lodge should be booked well in advance as it is the only in-fiord accommodation. Sandflies are prevalent at Milford Sound — bring strong insect repellent. November typically brings high rainfall to Milford Sound which actually enhances the waterfalls dramatically.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Kayak and Wilderness Walk Combo — an extraordinary full-day experience. Begin with a guided sea kayak paddle through the dramatic fiord at water level, passing beneath the towering 1,200-meter walls of Mitre Peak and Pembroke Glacier. Paddle to the base of Stirling Falls for an unforgettable close encounter with cascading water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the wilderness walk component — a guided walk through ancient Fiordland rainforest along the fiord edge, with expert interpretation of the unique Fiordland ecosystem. Spot fur seals, dolphins, and rare Fiordland crested penguins.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise on Milford Sound aboard a premium small vessel — champagne on deck as the last light catches the fiord walls. Return to the lodge for a final night in Milford Sound.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Milford Sound Lodge before the kayak departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch provided by the kayak operator, enjoyed on the fiord shore or a rocky beach accessible only by kayak
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Milford Sound Lodge — New Zealand blue cod, Bluff oysters (in season), and Central Otago wines

day_by_day.notes: The kayak and walk combo is best booked through Rosco's Milford Kayaks or a similar premium operator — request the small group or private guided option. Wetsuit and paddle gear is provided. The private sunset cruise can be arranged through Real Journeys or Cruise Milford — specify the premium small vessel option. November is an excellent month for Milford Sound as the waterfalls are at their most powerful.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Milford Sound after a leisurely breakfast and scenic drive back through Fiordland National Park to Te Anau. Stop at the Mirror Lakes and Eglinton Valley for photography — the reflections of the Earl Mountains on a still morning are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive north toward Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park via the Mackenzie Basin. Stop at Lake Pukaki for the iconic turquoise glacial lake views with Mount Cook on the horizon — one of New Zealand's most photographed landscapes. Check in at The Hermitage Hotel at Aoraki/Mount Cook — the legendary alpine lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into The Hermitage. Enjoy the hotel's renowned Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre for an immersive introduction to the mountain's history and the night sky planetarium show.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Milford Sound Lodge
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mackenzie's Restaurant, Lake Tekapo — lakeside dining with views of the turquoise lake and Church of the Good Shepherd
meals.dinner: The Hermitage's Panorama Restaurant — fine dining with direct floor-to-ceiling views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, featuring New Zealand high country lamb, Marlborough salmon, and an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Milford Sound to Aoraki/Mount Cook is approximately 5.5–6 hours including stops — depart Milford Sound by 9:00 AM. The Mackenzie Basin is a UNESCO Dark Sky Reserve — if skies are clear tonight, step outside the Hermitage for extraordinary stargazing. The Hermitage is the only full-service hotel within the national park and should be booked well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier — one of the South Island's most rewarding alpine hikes. Depart early from The Hermitage for the 10 km return walk through the heart of Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. Cross three swing bridges over glacial streams, pass the Mueller Glacier terminal lake, and arrive at the Hooker Lake viewpoint with Aoraki/Mount Cook towering directly ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to The Hermitage and enjoy the hotel's premium facilities — spa treatment, heated pool, or simply relax on the terrace with Mount Cook views. Optional afternoon glacier scenic flight by ski plane or helicopter over the Tasman Glacier and Mount Cook summit — the ultimate South Island aerial perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the Hermitage terrace or Kea Point lookout — the alpenglow on Aoraki/Mount Cook at dusk is an unforgettable sight. Elegant dinner at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at The Hermitage before the track departure — fuel up with a full cooked breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch from The Hermitage, enjoyed at the Hooker Lake viewpoint with Mount Cook as the backdrop
meals.dinner: The Hermitage Panorama Restaurant — premium degustation menu with New Zealand wine pairing; alternatively the more relaxed Old Guide's Restaurant for hearty post-hike fare

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is graded easy-moderate and is suitable after the multi-day Routeburn effort. Start early (7:00–8:00 AM) to have the track quieter and catch the morning light on the mountains. The glacier scenic flight is operated by Air Safaris or Mount Cook Ski Planes — book in advance and confirm weather the morning of. November offers long daylight hours — sunset is around 9:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Aoraki/Mount Cook and drive north through the Mackenzie Basin toward Hanmer Springs. Stop at Lake Tekapo for a visit to the Church of the Good Shepherd and the famous lupins in bloom along the lake shore (November is peak lupin season — an extraordinary purple and pink floral display against the turquoise lake).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hanmer Springs. Check in at a premium Hanmer Springs property such as The Heritage Hanmer Springs. Head directly to the Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools and Spa — soak tired hiking muscles in the geothermal mineral pools, enjoy private thermal pools, and book a premium spa treatment (hot stone massage or deep tissue recovery massage highly recommended after the Routeburn and Hooker Valley hikes).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in the charming alpine village of Hanmer Springs. Browse the boutique shops and enjoy a leisurely premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at The Hermitage before departure
meals.lunch: Kohan Japanese Restaurant, Lake Tekapo — an unexpected gem on the lake shore serving exceptional fresh Japanese cuisine with Tekapo views
meals.dinner: Coriander's Restaurant, Hanmer Springs — the finest dining in the village, offering New Zealand-inspired cuisine with an excellent wine list in a relaxed alpine atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Aoraki/Mount Cook to Hanmer Springs is approximately 3.5–4 hours. The lupins at Lake Tekapo typically peak in mid-to-late November — timing is perfect. Book the private thermal pool session and spa treatment at Hanmer Springs Thermal Pools in advance. Hanmer Springs is a genuinely relaxing contrast to the intense hiking days — embrace the slower pace.

day_by_day.morning: Morning leisure in Hanmer Springs — a final soak in the thermal pools or a guided forest walk through the Hanmer Forest Park. The Jack's Pass Road walk offers panoramic views over the Hanmer Basin and surrounding mountains — a gentle 2–3 hour return walk with minimal elevation gain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Hanmer Springs and drive to Christchurch (approximately 1.5 hours). Check in at a premium Christchurch hotel such as The George Christchurch or Otahuna Lodge (nearby). Explore the regenerated Christchurch city centre — the stunning Cardboard Cathedral, the Botanic Gardens in full spring bloom, and the vibrant Little High Eatery and Oxford Terrace precinct.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening of the South Island journey — celebrate with a premium dinner in Christchurch's thriving restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at The Heritage Hanmer Springs
meals.lunch: Riverside Market, Christchurch — a vibrant riverside food market with premium artisan food stalls, craft beer, and fresh produce
meals.dinner: Gatherings Restaurant, Christchurch — one of Canterbury's finest restaurants offering a seasonal tasting menu celebrating local South Island produce with matched Canterbury wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Christchurch Botanic Gardens are spectacular in November with spring flowers in full bloom — allow time for a walk through. The George Christchurch is the city's most celebrated boutique luxury hotel and is ideally located for exploring the city. Consider booking a private e-bike tour of the Christchurch city centre and Hagley Park for a fun afternoon exploration option.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Christchurch. Leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute exploration of Christchurch — visit the Re:START Mall, the Canterbury Museum, or take a punting on the Avon River experience through the Botanic Gardens for a quintessentially Christchurch farewell.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final New Zealand lunch and transfer to Christchurch International Airport for departure. Private luxury transfer from hotel to airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Christchurch International Airport. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day South Island journey encompassing world-class hiking, New Zealand's highest bungy jump, fiord kayaking, glacier views, and thermal relaxation.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at The George Christchurch — enjoy every last bite of New Zealand's exceptional produce
meals.lunch: Twenty Seven Steps Restaurant, Christchurch — elegant heritage building dining with a seasonal New Zealand menu, perfect for a refined farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — request premium meal options if available on the departure flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security at Christchurch International Airport. New Zealand has strict biosecurity rules — ensure no fresh food, soil, or plant material is packed in luggage. Consider purchasing last-minute New Zealand souvenirs at the Christchurch Airport premium retail area. Review any duty-free allowances for your destination country.
